text_post: The thing is sex is the most intimate thing 2 (or more!) human beings can do together, nothing else comes close. So when there is a connection between 2 people, a genuine affection, a real bond or fondness for one another, then sex acts as a way to make that affection real, vital, it takes it to another level. I am willfully friendless, or nearly so rather. I have one friend, and that's fine. I am less lonely in my own company, and in the company of my building's cats, listening to music. I regret so many so-called friendships. I would have been better off reading, watching the birds, listening to music. That doesn't mean I am not lonely, or less lonely now than I was decades ago, because that is certainly not the case; but if I got caught up in superficial social relations again, I would be more frustrated, bitter. I am not going to make that mistake again.  Still, I don't see how a deep, aching loneliness can be avoided if you are not making love (note I write 'making love', not 'fucking' although fucking certainly has its place) to somebody in the prime of your life, on a regular basis. It's not natural living like a monk/nun. There is no getting away from that. And there is a price to pay for such lack of physical, sexual intimacy with another human being. A terrible price I would not wish on my worst enemy.
